title: Scott Joplin at Atlantic City and Alonzo Hardy
summary: White says he knew Joplin, who brought four rags to the Jenkins band at Atlantic City and gave them to bandmaster Alonzo Hardy.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Knew him personally. Knew him personally. Knew him personally.

He came to the band in Atlantic City while we were engaged on the boardwalk there. Young's Million Dollar Pear in Atlantic City was where the Jenkins band was playing. When Scott Joplin walked out and brought his rag. The Maple Leaf Rag. Right. Then he brought- The first I ever heard of the Bolo Rag. Sweet Meats. And then I don't know whether he wrote Temptation or not but those four were the featured rags with the band.
Well now when I went to New Orleans I started putting that double beat on it like that.

We used to play it like a ragtime should be played. You see. Ought to be played those days. Of course the boys in New Orleans put a different touch on it. Scott Joplin presented Alonzo Hardy with the Maple Leaf Rag and these other three rags there and told him, well you can have these if you're playing for me. And Alonzo issued the parts out and said, well, we'll have to play it for you. Because there wasn't anything too tough for Alonzo Hardy. He was the first bandmaster I had been in the college. John Brown succeeded him. I succeeded John Brown. Of course they expelled me. Dr. Osmond told me the college could never do without you the next year. But Alonzo Hardy was our bandmaster and a great bandmaster. See he became bandmaster in the 15th Regiment of New York in his latter years. And he died in New York. They told me, so they told me that he drank everything. I wouldn't doubt it.
